posts.caption: In 2021, one engineer typed one wrong command and 3.5 billion people lost the internet in a single instant. Not hacked. Not attacked. Just one wrong line of code during a routine maintenance check. Facebook's own engineers couldn't even log in to fix it, their access tools were on the same servers that just vanished. They had to physically drive to data centers and override servers by hand. One by one. 6 hours. $60 million lost every single hour. And the exact same vulnerability? Still exists right now. The internet is more fragile than you think.

2021 mein ek engineer ne ek galat command type ki aur 3.5 billion logon ka internet ek pal mein band ho gaya. Hack nahi hua. Attack nahi hua. Bas ek routine maintenance check ke dauran ek galat line of code. 6 ghante. Har ghante 60 million dollar ka nuksaan. Internet utna strong nahi jitna hum sochte hain.

There is a sound that only 2% of people can hear. Scientists have studied it for 50 years and still have no answer. It's called The Hum — and the leading theory is that it's the Earth itself vibrating at a frequency most humans aren't built to detect. A woman heard it for 11 years, moved across the country to escape it, and it followed her to the new house. Stop right now, close your eyes, and listen. What do you hear?

We call space the final frontier. But we've barely explored our own planet. Earth is stranger than anything we've found out there — and most people have no idea. From perfect solar eclipses to oceans deeper than mountains are tall, this is the planet you thought you knew.

In 1974, a man calculated the exact day he would die and spent a year preparing for it. What happened next is stranger than the prediction itself. Frank was obsessed with numerology. He told his family, quit his job, and gave away everything he owned. When the day came and went without incident, he thought he'd beaten fate. He hadn't.

The perfect reminder that every destination has its own unique way of life. 🌍⁠
A common sight in Lombok, Indonesia, where locals sell gasoline in bottles for scooter riders.⁠
⁠
With scooters being one of the most popular ways to get around the island, these roadside fuel stands offer a simple and convenient solution that you won't often see in big cities.⁠
⁠
A small cultural detail that says a lot about local life.⁠
🎥: @fulltimetrippin

By day, the eastern quoll looks like a small, spotted marsupial. Under ultraviolet light, its fur reveals a completely different side, glowing in vivid shades that are invisible to the human eye.⁠
⁠
This is biofluorescence, a form of “living light” in which an animal absorbs light from its surroundings and re-emits it at a different wavelength. Unlike bioluminescence, the animal does not produce the light itself.⁠
⁠
The purpose of this glow is still a mystery. It may have a role in communication

Some hotels are more than just a place to sleep.⁠
⁠
Across the world, travelers can find stays inside a retired airplane, beneath the ocean, above the rainforest, and even inside structures made from natural materials like ice.⁠
⁠
These places turn a simple overnight stay into an experience worth traveling for.⁠
⁠
Which one would you spend a night in?⁠
⁠
By: @faraldacranehotel @icehotelsweden @bookandbedtokyo @hotelcostaverde @hotel_jested_official @tubohotel @huilohuilo_biologicalreserve @v8hot

A food journey through Osaka, Japan, a city known as the “Kitchen of Japan.” 🍣⁠
⁠
From traditional robatayaki and fresh unagi to sizzling yakiniku, okonomiyaki, and famous street-style dishes, Osaka offers endless flavors waiting to be discovered.⁠
⁠
These 7 spots are perfect for anyone looking to experience the city through its food culture, where every meal tells a story.⁠
⁠
Would you add Osaka to your foodie bucket list?⁠
🎥: @my_season___

@amsterdam_special & @when.in.amsterdam captured this famous tree tunnel in the Netherlands across different seasons.⁠
⁠
Located in Amsterdam’s Oud-Zuid neighborhood, Lomanstraat is known for the tall trees lining both sides of the street. Over the years, their branches have grown toward each other, creating the natural canopy that makes the street so recognizable.⁠
⁠
The scene changes throughout the year, from a lush green tunnel in summer to warm golden tones in autumn.⁠
⁠

This Maldives experiment is everything. 🌊✨⁠
⁠
@mermaid.kayleigh attached a light underwater and watched as whale sharks gathered around it, creating an incredible encounter with the world's largest fish.⁠
⁠
A fascinating reminder of how curious these gentle giants can be. 🐋💙

Matmata is home to a remarkable style of architecture that has been part of local life for centuries.⁠
⁠
Berber communities created homes around large courtyards dug into the ground, with rooms set into the surrounding earth.⁠
⁠
Matmata later became famous around the world as a filming location for Star Wars: A New Hope, with Hotel Sidi Driss serving as Luke Skywalker’s childhood home.⁠
⁠
By: @mustafaa7⁠

@thelosttwo showed us a hotel room with one of the most breathtaking views in China. ⁠
⁠
Overlooking Guilin’s famous karst mountains, this stay combines floor-to-ceiling windows, an infinity pool, and landscapes that look almost too perfect to be real.⁠
A room where the view becomes the main attraction. 🏞️⁠
⁠
Would you wake up to this every morning?

Ever had dinner inside a restaurant made entirely of ice and snow? ⁠
⁠
The Hôtel de Glace Restaurant in Québec brings this unusual winter experience to life each season, with an icy dining room and a three-course meal created by the chefs at Fairmont Le Château Frontenac.⁠
⁠
Who would you bring here for dinner? 👀⁠
⁠
By: @hoteldeglace @fairmontfrontenac

If you want to properly refresh in Naples, now you know how it’s done. 🍋😆⁠
⁠
@doctor_pao_ showed us a local lemonade vendor with a serving style that's impossible to forget. Expect plenty of lemon, plenty of laughs, and maybe a little splash too.⁠

For juvenile Kemp’s ridley sea turtles like Lucky, warming oceans can carry them farther north than expected. But when temperatures drop in these northern waters, the cold can leave them unable to swim, increasing the risk of strandings far from their tropical habitat.

Learn more about Lucky and other cold-stunned turtles at the link in bio. 

Video by Atlantis Paradise Island, Bahamas

Photograph by @mitchell.leong | Bathed in the soft glow of the rising sun, a mountain goat stands tall amid a vibrant meadow of wildflowers in the Canadian Rockies. The stillness was broken only by the rustling flowers, buzzing bees, and occasional whispering wind. It was an unparalleled moment in a vast wilderness that felt both eternal and fragile.

This photo was featured in our #NatGeoYourShotOurHOME challenge.

On September 11, 2001, first responders, co-workers, and strangers were brought together through unbelievable acts of bravery and community. Now, 25 years later, they have a chance to reunite for the first time and say thank you. 

#911Reunited is now streaming on @DisneyPlus and @hulu.

It's hungry work being this adorable, but Mom is happy to provide. Ordinarily, in meerkat clans, only the dominant female and her partner are allowed to mate. Others in the group are tasked with rearing her young and teaching them to hunt, groom each other, and defend the clan. While the social structure is complex, it's a cooperative way of life that's becoming more important as the Kalahari grows hotter and drier. 

Learn why powerful matriarchs are vital to meerkat survival at the link in bio

Kio has a big future ahead of him, and #NatGeoLION captured it all.

Take a behind-the-scenes look at his extraordinary true journey with executive producers Jon Favreau and Mike Gunton. Now streaming on @DisneyPlus and @hulu.

In Kisumu, Kenya, thousands of people are working together to change the way HIV prevention is viewed. By making medical care more accessible and challenging the stigma around PrEP, advocates are not only helping to save lives but also empowering women at increased risk to take control of their health. Join National Geographic Explorer and photographer @renaeffendiphoto who traveled to the city to see their impact firsthand. 

Learn more about HIV prevention in Kenya at the link in bio. | @gilea

While living in a fishing village on Mexico’s Baja California peninsula, photographer @nicolas.hahn noticed that the midday winds pushed all kinds of sea creatures close to shore. During one snorkeling session, he discovered this remarkable scene: a collection of mauve stingers, a type of small bioluminescent jellyfish. Hahn got stung a few times around his mask, but the pain was worth it as his underwater lens captured every last tentacle in astonishing detail.

Ancient ancestors of the dolphin hid from the sun’s UV rays using two light-detecting spots. Fascinatingly, some inherited mutations that allowed them to perceive light and shade together, so they could visualise their environment - essentially becoming the first proper eyes.

Dogs move differently to humans. They have a digitigrade posture, which means they walk on their toe bones. This anatomy allows longer and more efficient strides so they run faster and jump further. With less surface area touching the ground, they also move with more agility and greater stealth.
